body: This conflicts with main. Please run /resolve-conflicts (or git merge upstream/main, keep both sides) and push. The usual cause is that both sides added lines in the same place.

Main is merged into the branch (`9b2b4851`), and the `needs-rework` review items are done in `5237db06`.

**Merge:** one plain merge of `origin/main` (`5fd45923`), no rebase, no force-push. Main's one-pick rule (#692) had removed `pick_face`/`pick_edge`/`hover_feature_at` and `hover_vertex`/`pick_vertex` while this branch added wcs branches inside them, so those two files (interact.rs, vertex_pick.rs) take main's version and the wcs branches are re-homed in main's `feature_click::ask` — with `centres: false` in the wcs `PickKinds` (step 2's centre picks stay out of the role law: a role never takes an arc centre). Every other conflict kept both sides. `wcs_pick::arm` now disarms `points_pick` and vice versa, like the other mutual-exclusive modes.

**Review items:**
- The five clippy hits are cleared: the collapsible nested `if` in `pick/roles.rs` is a let-chain; the four `needless_range_loop`s are the fixed 3×3 Jacobi rotation — that loop nest is the algorithm's shape, so it keeps a scoped `#[allow]` with a comment rather than mangling the math.
- `pick/roles.rs` was 477 lines, over the 400-line law: `fit_wall`, `perp_basis` and `jacobi_sym3` (and their constants) move to a new `pick/wall_fit.rs`; roles.rs is now 283 lines.

Gates: `wcs_roles` 6/6, app lib 107/107, ui lib 461 passed (5 GPU tests ignored headless), `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Ready for a re-check.

The correctness blocker is fixed, red test first, plus a drive-by on a gate that was already red on main. Head is `e36c9d08`.

**Blocker - the first axis used raw:** fixed in `816ed931`, at the read site as asked. `a` is normalised right after `datum_for` returns it: `a_len = norm(a)`, a zero or non-finite length is refused by name (`"{} of '{}' has no length - re-pick it"`, the same idiom `straight_edge` uses), then `scale(a, 1.0 / a_len)` puts a unit vector in the frame. The `Datum.dir` doc comment now says what is true: a straight edge's direction is its raw walk, and `align_roles` normalises it before use.

**Red pin first:** `5de8c124` adds a 46-line test to `crates/app/tests/wcs_roles.rs` - a 20x20x10 block pitched 25 deg about X, Z = the vertical 10 mm edge, X = the +X side face - asserting orthonormal axes and the expected 25 deg roll. Pre-fix it reproduces your numbers: `y = [-0.0, 9.063, 4.226]`, roll 45.56 deg. Post-fix, green.

**Merge:** one plain merge of `origin/main` (`2b15cf83`, main at `77b897c8`). No rebase, no force-push.

**Drive-by (flagging, happy to drop):** the seam-law gate `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam` is red on clean `origin/main` - `refusal_ghost.rs:44` prints its budget warning directly (it landed that way via `90e3be04`). That gate runs in this PR's lane, so `e36c9d08` fixes it here: one line, `eprintln!` -> `diag_warn!`. Say the word if you would rather carry it as its own PR and I will drop the commit.

**Local results at head `e36c9d08`:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 7 passed (the six plus the new pin) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 108 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` | 531 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |

The MCP follow-up you suggested is filed as #937 and named in the body. (One heads-up: outside contributors cannot set labels here, so #937 was created unlabelled - the requested `area:mcp`, P1 and `source:agent` will need a maintainer's triage.)

Fixed the blocker, and merged current `main` in — head is now `d2663a3f`.

**The blocker** — done your way (option (a)): Apply only answers on the **active** setup's row. `CommandKind::SetWcs` places the active setup's WCS, so the row now gates itself against `setup::active` live: on a row whose setup isn't active, Apply is greyed and its hover tip says "Make Setup1 the active setup to set its WCS from features" (naming the setup that would receive the placement). The gate deliberately isn't `enabled = draft.is_ready()` — it ANDs in the active-setup check, so a ready draft on a dormant row can't fire.

New pin: `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::the_row_on_an_inactive_setup_cannot_move_another_setups_work_zero` follows your repro shape exactly — Setup1 active, the draft sits on Setup2's row, Apply is greyed (hover words pinned, `query_by_label_contains`), and the harness `pending` queue is shown empty so nothing can be sent; then `ActivateSetup(Setup2)` on the same row places Setup2's WCS at `[20.0, 20.0, 10.0]` — the same frame your repro measured — while Setup1's work zero stays `None`, untouched.

**Notes 37–41:**
- 37 (MCP parity): filed as #937 ("MCP: set WCS from feature picks", `area:mcp`, P1) and named in the body's Follow-ups; the MCP `set_wcs` still takes only the absolute origin/quaternion until that lands.
- 38 (wall sidedness): added to the body's Follow-ups — the hemisphere rule is deterministic today, but siding a wall axis by the origin pick (like edges) would match what a user expects.
- 39 (origin sentence): the body's App-lane paragraph now reads "without one, the origin falls on the second axis pick's anchor (an edge's start, a face's centroid, a wall's centre), projected onto the first pick's plane when that pick is a face" — matching the code.
- 40 (`e36c9d08` vs #908): confirmed — the merge with current main folds it in cleanly, nothing else to do.
- 41 (stale test counts): the body's Tested section is refreshed to the merged head `d2663a3f` (the numbers below), and the stale "lathe_thread_travel broken on main" note is dropped — `--all-targets` now compiles clean.

**Tested at the merged head** (`d2663a3f`, contains `origin/main` `f490458a`): `wcs_roles` 7 passed, app lib 110 passed, full `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` 538 passed / 5 ignored, `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Body updated: new origin sentence, the active-setup gate in the UI-lane paragraph, the two-setup pin named in Pins, and the wall-sidedness follow-up.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d2663a3f8d954649a051d8bfa7268b03938def06 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The round-3 blocker (Apply moving the active setup's WCS) is fixed. But a Z pick plus a Y pick builds a rotated frame: the Y pick comes out as X and the Z pick as Y. Our earlier rounds missed this, and I am sorry it turns up this late.

Thank you @tbrasselle. The inactive-setup fix is the small, safe option, and its pin is exactly the one we asked for.

**Earlier blocker (review at `e36c9d08`)**
- **Apply on another setup's row moved the ACTIVE setup's WCS: fixed** in `9645bee6`. `wcs_pick_row.rs:75` compares the row's setup with `setup::active`, and Apply stays grey (`:96`) with the plain hover text "Make Setup2 the active setup to set its WCS from features". The draft keeps its picks. `align_roles` reads them through `view_pose` (the active setup's frame), so once the row's setup is active, the picks and the placed WCS are read in the same frame. The new pin, `the_row_on_an_inactive_setup_cannot_move_another_setups_work_zero`, has two setups and the row on the inactive one. It asserts that nothing is queued while the setup is inactive, that the active setup's work zero never moves, and that the row's own setup lands on the picked corner once it is active. It passes here.
- MCP/script path: this PR adds no MCP tool. The existing `set_wcs` takes an absolute pose. The follow-up is named in the body (#937), which satisfies the rule.

**New blocker**
1. **The (Z, Y) role pair builds the wrong frame.** `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:138-141`:
   ```rust
   (Role::Z, Role::Y) => {
       let x = square_to(g2, d2.dir, a, tilt)?;   // this is the Y pick's direction
       (x, a, cross(x, a))                        // X <- Y pick, Y <- Z pick
   }
   ```
   `AXIS_PRIORITY` is `[Z, X, Y]`, so a Z pick with a Y pick always takes this arm, in either pick order. The frame is right-handed and orthonormal, so every finiteness and handedness check passes. But it is turned 120 degrees about the diagonal: the WCS's +X lies along the picked Y edge, its +Y along the face normal, and its +Z along the part's +X. Every posted coordinate from that WCS would be wrong. Reproduction (a local test, not pushed) on the plain 20x20x10 `block(0.0)` from `wcs_roles.rs`: top face as Z, edge (0,0,10)-(0,20,10) as Y, corner (0,0,10) as Origin:
   ```
   x [0.0, 1.0, 0.0] y [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] z [1.0, 0.0, 0.0] pos [0.0, 0.0, 10.0] rpy 90 0 90
   panicked: Y pick sets Y
   ```
   Expected: x = (1,0,0), y = (0,1,0), z = (0,0,1), rpy 0 0 0.
   Fix: `let y = square_to(g2, d2.dir, a, tilt)?; (cross(y, a), y, a)`. The arms `(X, Z)`, `(Y, Z)` and `(Y, X)` cannot be reached under this priority. Please either drop them, or check them the same way, because `(Y, Z)` and `(X, Z)` are only right by luck of their names. Please pin the fix with a (Z, Y) test, and ideally a loop over every reachable pair on a skewed part that asserts each pick's role axis equals its own pick direction. Today nothing in `wcs_roles.rs` or `wcs_pick_tests.rs` uses a Z+Y pair, which is how this got past the tests.

**What I tried on the frame maths** (local tests on a block placed at (3,-4,5) and rotated roll 25 / pitch -11 / yaw 37; not pushed)
- (Z,X), (X,Y), with and without an origin pick: unit, mutually orthogonal and right-handed to 1e-9, with the picked axes on the part's own edge and face directions. The Euler angles handed to `SetWcs` round-trip back to the same three columns through `quat_from_euler` to 1e-9.
- Each of these is refused with a named message, never a NaN frame or a silent fallback: the same edge as X and Y; two parallel edges; the same face as Z and X; a vertical edge as X against the top face as Z ("too near parallel to the first axis"); a vertex as an axis.
- An origin with only ONE axis is refused ("set the WCS from two axes ..."). That is safe, but the "Pick for WCS" hover text says "Two axes, or an axis and an origin, place the WCS" (`wcs_pick_row.rs:39`), and the two-pick refusal says the same. Please make the text match the law (two axes, plus an optional origin). This is not blocking.
- Work offset: nothing here derives G54-G59. Apply queues the existing undoable `SetWcs`, and `setup::wcs_slot` stays the only source.

**Local results** (PR head merged with `origin/main` `23c62044`; the merge is clean)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 7 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib wcs_pick` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 8 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib structural` | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| reviewer's local (Z,Y) repro | **fails**, see above |

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:138-141`: fix the (Z, Y) arm as above, and pin it with a test.

**Notes (non-blocking)**
- `wall_datum` (`roles.rs:276`) falls back to an identity pose with `view_pose(...).unwrap_or_default()`, and it silently drops facet ids it cannot find (`filter_map(|i| tris.get(..))`). A missing pose or facet would be better refused by name, like the other datums.
- The earlier notes about the wall axis sign rule and about the body's origin wording still stand.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
